paras: The killing of Monroe was the shooting of a Black man named Monroe by a bailiff in Clayton County, Georgia, on March 15, 1882, while the bailiff tried to arrest him and another Black man, John Brown, on a charge of theft or forgery. Brown escaped and was captured weeks later at a railroad job in Monroe County, and the episode reached print mainly as a story about his arrest.

According to the Monroe Advertiser, Monroe and Brown were "charged with stealing goods or forging an order for them." The paper did not say which charge applied, and it named neither the bailiff nor the place in Clayton County where the attempted arrest happened.

When the bailiff came into the store where the two men were, they "dodged out" and he followed them outside. In the paper's telling, Monroe had a pistol drawn, Brown seized it from him and fired at the bailiff, and the bailiff "fired back and killed Monroe." Brown then fled, and this version of the shooting is the only one in the coverage.

Officers suspected Brown had gone toward Monroe County, and Sheriff King of that county learned that he was working on the railroad at the mouth of the Towaliga River. Carrying a warrant from the sheriff of Clayton with orders to "take him at all hazards," King found Brown holding up a timber for a trestle and handcuffed him before he could move. The Clayton sheriff then took Brown back to Jonesboro.
No report of an inquest into Monroe's death, of any inquiry into the bailiff, or of Brown's trial appears in the coverage.

The Savannah Morning News reprinted the Monroe Advertiser item on April 13, 1882, in its "Georgia Affairs" column among items on a chicken fight, a gin fire and a store burglary. The item gave Monroe's death a single clause and spent most of its length on Brown's capture, told with humor: his "heart smote him" as the sheriff approached and "the iron bracelets were on him" before he understood. It accepted the bailiff's account without comment, and no other newspaper report of the shooting was found.

reader.title: Killing of Monroe by a Clayton County bailiff
bases: A bailiff shot and killed Monroe while trying to arrest him and John Brown on a theft or forgery charge; no crowd or mob is mentioned (A1).
The only report is one Monroe Advertiser item, reprinted in the Savannah Morning News (A1).

accounts.label: Monroe Advertiser (reprinted)
accounts.gist: The two men dodged out of a store when the bailiff approached; outside, Monroe had a pistol drawn, Brown seized it and fired at the bailiff, and the bailiff fired back and killed Monroe. The paper names no source; the account matches the officer's side and no other version appears.

framing.detail: A brief item in a column of state news, mostly about Brown's capture, told with humor ('his heart smote him', 'the iron bracelets were on him'); the killing of Monroe gets one clause and no comment.

record_check.record: John Brown seized the bailiff's pistol during the arrest; the bailiff fired back
record_check.dossier: Brown seized Monroe's pistol (not the bailiff's) and fired at the bailiff; the bailiff fired back

record_check.record: Brown arrested by Sheriff King at a railroad work site
record_check.dossier: Supported; King was sheriff of Monroe county, acting on a Clayton warrant, at the mouth of the Towaliga river

info: Outside a store in Clayton county; no town named
Monroe, described as a 'negro' (only one name given)

sources.note: 'Georgia Affairs' column reprints a Monroe Advertiser item: on March 15 a Clayton county bailiff killed Monroe while arresting him and John Brown; Brown later arrested by Sheriff King at the mouth of the Towaliga river.
quotes: On the 15th of March last a bailiff in Cleyton county undertook to arrest John Brown and another negro named Monroe, who were charged with stealing goods or forging an order for them.
Brown, however, seized the pistol out of his companion's hard and fired at the bailiff, and the bailiff fired back and killed Monroe.
Mr. King armed himself with a warrant from the Sheriff of Clayton, accompanied by the instruction to 'take him at all hazards.'

acts.note: Bailiff tried to arrest Monroe and Brown; they dodged out of the store.
Bailiff fired back and killed Monroe after Brown, with Monroe's pistol, fired at him.
Sheriff King captured Brown at a railroad job; date given only as weeks later.
